_about: The outside standards OpenEMR answers to, for motion's conformance lens: each ONC certification criterion OpenEMR 8 is certified for (from its CHPL listing) (and a few standards it isn't certified for but still implements), the code paths that carry it, the official tool that tests it and whether that tool can run on a PR before merge, and what the pending HTI-5 rule would do to it. A PR is matched by its files or its title. Paths are this file's reading of the code, not the certification documents', so every entry says mapping: provisional until a maintainer confirms it. Privacy and security criteria are listed so PRs reach the right reviewers, never analysed.
heading: The standards OpenEMR is certified against

source.certification: OpenEMR 8, CHPL 15.05.05.3115.OPEN.02.01.1.260130, certified 2026-01-30 by SLI Compliance, status Active
source.criteria_from: its CHPL listing, read through the CHPL API (32 criteria; OpenEMR's wiki lists the same)
source.official_findings: CHPL records 0 surveillance activities, 0 non-conformities (open or closed) and 0 direct reviews for this listing.
source.methods: CHPL also records how each criterion was certified: by ONC test procedure with a test tool, by gap certification through a 2025 attestation (not re-tested), or by attestation alone. Each is a permitted method; attestation means no test result stands behind the criterion.

rule.name: HTI-5
rule.text: ASTP/ONC's HTI-5 proposed rule (published 2025-12-29, comments closed 2026-02-27) would remove 34 of the 60 certification criteria, revise 7 and keep 19. Some removals take effect on the final rule's effective date, others on 2027-01-01. No final rule had been published when this was checked.

tool.name: Inferno (g)(10) test kit
tool.note: Core runs it in CI (.github/workflows/inferno-test.yml) only where the INFERNO_PAT secret is available: master and maintainers' own branches, not PRs from forks. The 2026-10-20 weekly meeting: it "only runs when code reaches master".

specs.security_note: Authorization, scopes and token handling are the maintainers' security review (the FHIR and OAuth test work Brady described on 2026-10-20). This map labels them; it doesn't analyse them.

guidance.text: A server's CapabilityStatement (its /metadata) declares the interactions and search parameters it supports, and clients rely on it. Advertising _sort or _count where they aren't implemented makes a client get unsorted or unpaged results without an error.
